text:
Philip Broberg sits at the very top of NHL Edge's top-speed charts for defensemen and forwards alike, and this season the Blues have handed him the keys. He's playing 24:35 a night, more than 26 minutes over his last 10, and he's on the ice for 49% of St. Louis's power-play chances, up from 28% last year. The result is 14 points in 21 games and a breakout flag from us: 0.67 points a game against 0.42 last season, with his own chances up from 0.24 expected goals per 60 to 0.39.

Some of it will cool. He's shooting 11.6% against a talent range of about 7%, and the Blues have scored 9.6 goals more than expected with him on the ice. The underlying skater is real, though: Evolving-Hockey had him 20th of 215 defensemen in wins above replacement last season, with four goals of value just from drawing more penalties than he takes, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 95th percentile for chances from the home-plate area. He left Saturday's game against Florida as a precaution and scored in his return Tuesday.
